title: Single-phase supply, meter and consumer unit

circuit.name: Single-phase supply, meter and consumer unit

components.label: 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V

activities.title: Inspect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V
activities.instruction: Choose 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: This is where power enters the bench. Follow the line, neutral and earth from here.

activities.title: Inspect Electricity meter
activities.instruction: Choose Electricity meter, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: A supply meter records energy in kilowatt-hours. Its practice display shows the power passing through its own line connection right now, in kilowatts (kW).

activities.title: Inspect Main switch
activities.instruction: Choose Main switch, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: One handle disconnects both line and neutral.

activities.title: Inspect Distribution board
activities.instruction: Choose Distribution board, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: Open the door to reach the breakers. Behind the front panel are the rails, wires and terminal bars.

activities.title: Inspect Lamp circuit breaker (MCB)
activities.instruction: Choose Lamp circuit breaker (MCB), then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: A circuit breaker trips if too much current flows. A heavy fault can trip it quickly. A smaller overload can take longer.

activities.title: Inspect Lamp on the outgoing circuit
activities.instruction: Choose Lamp on the outgoing circuit, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: The lamp gets brighter as it draws more power. Measure from L to N to check the voltage across it.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: You open the main switch. What happens to the light?
activities.explanation: The meter records how much electricity you use. Turning off the main switch cuts power to the board. The wires feeding the switch can still be live.

options.label: It goes out
It stays on while the meter has power

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · L to Electricity meter · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · L to Electricity meter · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Electricity meter · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Electricity meter · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to Electricity meter · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to Electricity meter · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter.

activities.title: Connect Electricity meter · LOUT to Main switch · LIN
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Electricity meter · LOUT to Main switch · LIN with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Load side of the meter. Follow L through to LIN. → Incoming L terminal. Follow it to LOUT on the other side of the same pole.

activities.title: Connect Electricity meter · NOUT to Main switch · NIN
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Electricity meter · NOUT to Main switch · NIN with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Load side of the meter. Follow N through to NIN. → Incoming neutral terminal. Follow it to NOUT on the other side of the same pole.

activities.title: Connect Main switch · LOUT to Distribution board · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Main switch · LOUT to Distribution board · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal. Follow it to LIN on the other side of the same pole. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Main switch · NOUT to Distribution board · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Main switch · NOUT to Distribution board · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing neutral terminal. Follow it to NIN on the other side of the same pole. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Electricity meter · PEOUT to Distribution board · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Electricity meter · PEOUT to Distribution board · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect Distribution board · LOUT to Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Distribution board · LOUT to Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 1 with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal. Follow it to LIN on the other side of the same pole. → Top 1 takes the line feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked 2.

activities.title: Connect Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 2 to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 2 to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Distribution board · NOUT to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Distribution board · NOUT to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing neutral terminal. Follow it to NIN on the other side of the same pole. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Distribution board · PEOUT to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Distribution board · PEOUT to Lamp on the outgoing circuit · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Check the circuit with the control on
activities.instruction: Check the circuit with the control on.
activities.explanation: Lamp on the outgoing circuit draws power.

expectedObservations.title: Lamp on the outgoing circuit draws power

activities.title: Open the main switch
activities.instruction: Turn Main switch off.
activities.explanation: Lamp on the outgoing circuit stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: Lamp on the outgoing circuit stops drawing power

activities.title: Close the main switch
activities.instruction: Turn Main switch on.
activities.explanation: Lamp on the outgoing circuit draws power.

expectedObservations.title: Lamp on the outgoing circuit draws power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Lamp on the outgoing circuit · L and the black probe on Lamp on the outgoing circuit · N. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Compare line to neutral before and after the main switch. With that switch open, its supply side can still read close to mains voltage. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Electricity meter · L. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Lamp circuit breaker (MCB) · 2 and Lamp on the outgoing circuit · L. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Which device turned off the supply to the board?
activities.explanation: The meter records how much electricity you use. Turning off the main switch cuts power to the board. The wires feeding the switch can still be live.

options.label: The meter
The main switch

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Single-phase supply, meter and consumer unit
challenge.briefing: The meter has a supply but the lamp is dark.
challenge.hint: Start at the outgoing breaker. Compare its output with the line terminal at the lamp.
challenge.answer: The wire from the breaker output to lamp L is open. Voltage at the meter tells you the incoming supply is present, but it doesn’t tell you that the lamp has a complete circuit.

activities.instruction: Choose Shared RCCB · residual current only, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: This device compares the current in line and neutral. If some returns another way, it can trip. A separate breaker or fuse protects against overload.

activities.instruction: Choose Outgoing MCB 1, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: A circuit breaker trips if too much current flows. A heavy fault can trip it quickly. A smaller overload can take longer.

activities.instruction: Choose Lamp on breaker 1, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.

activities.title: Inspect Outgoing MCB 2
activities.instruction: Choose Outgoing MCB 2, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: A circuit breaker trips if too much current flows. A heavy fault can trip it quickly. A smaller overload can take longer.

activities.title: Inspect Socket on breaker 2
activities.instruction: Choose Socket on breaker 2, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: A double socket with an appliance plugged into the circuit. Both earth terminals share one metal strap.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: You switch off the lamp breaker. What else loses power?
activities.explanation: Follow the two wires leaving the breakers. One goes to the lamp and the other to the socket. The RCCB is their shared trip switch.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · L to Shared RCCB · residual current only · 1 with the line (L) wire.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Shared RCCB · residual current only · 3
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Shared RCCB · residual current only · 3 with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. → Top 3 takes the neutral feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked 4.

activities.title: Connect Shared RCCB · residual current only · 2 to Outgoing MCB 1 · 1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Shared RCCB · residual current only · 2 to Outgoing MCB 1 · 1 with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Top 1 takes the line feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked 2.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Outgoing MCB 1 · 2 to Lamp on breaker 1 · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Shared RCCB · residual current only · 4 to Lamp on breaker 1 · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Shared RCCB · residual current only · 4 to Lamp on breaker 1 · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 4 carries neutral out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 3. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to Lamp on breaker 1 · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to Lamp on breaker 1 · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect Shared RCCB · residual current only · 2 to Outgoing MCB 2 · 1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Shared RCCB · residual current only · 2 to Outgoing MCB 2 · 1 with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Top 1 takes the line feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked 2.

activities.title: Connect Outgoing MCB 2 · 2 to Socket on breaker 2 · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Outgoing MCB 2 · 2 to Socket on breaker 2 · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Shared RCCB · residual current only · 4 to Socket on breaker 2 · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Shared RCCB · residual current only · 4 to Socket on breaker 2 · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 4 carries neutral out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 3. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to Socket on breaker 2 · E
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to Socket on breaker 2 · E with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → The metal strap joins both earth terminals. Either terminal connects to the same earth path.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Try the lamp and socket together
activities.instruction: Try the lamp and socket together.
activities.explanation: Lamp on breaker 1 draws power. Socket on breaker 2 draws power.

activities.title: Switch off the first breaker
activities.instruction: Turn Outgoing MCB 1 off.
activities.explanation: Lamp on breaker 1 stops drawing power. The other circuit stays on.

expectedObservations.title: Lamp on breaker 1 stops drawing power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Lamp on breaker 1 · L and the black probe on Lamp on breaker 1 · N. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Compare the voltage across each load with MCB 1 off. A current reading on the RCCB feed includes both branches that are running. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Shared RCCB · residual current only · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Why does the socket still have power?
activities.explanation: Follow the two wires leaving the breakers. One goes to the lamp and the other to the socket. The RCCB is their shared trip switch.

options.label: Its own breaker and the RCCB are both still on
The lamp breaker switches only the neutral

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Shared RCCB with outgoing MCB circuits
challenge.briefing: A fault on one circuit has tripped the shared device. Both loads are off.
challenge.hint: Find the device that feeds both breakers. Does it show a trip?
challenge.answer: Current is leaking to earth at the lamp load. The shared RCCB detects the imbalance and opens, cutting power to both branches.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Measure across each lamp
activities.instruction: Measure across each lamp.
activities.explanation: Hall light A draws power. Hall light B draws power. Hall light C draws power. All three lamps have nearly the same voltage.

expectedObservations.title: All three lamps have nearly the same voltage

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Hall light A · L and the black probe on Hall light A · N. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Read L to N at each lit lamp. Each should be close to the full supply. The shared feed carries the current for all the lamps that are on. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load and Hall light B · N. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Where does each lamp get its voltage?
activities.explanation: Each lamp has its own path from the switched line to neutral. Electricians call that a parallel circuit.

options.label: Between the same switched line and neutral
Across one part of a chain of three lamps

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Parallel lighting bank
challenge.briefing: One lamp is dark. The two beside it still work.
challenge.hint: Compare the dark lamp’s line and neutral connections with the working lamps.
challenge.answer: Lamp B has an open neutral wire. The other two branches still have complete return paths, so their lamps can stay on.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply

activities.title: Turn off switch A

challenge.title: Diagnose: Two-gang independent lighting zones
challenge.briefing: Both lighting zones have gone out and the device feeding them has tripped.
challenge.hint: Look at what protects both zones, then check which branch has the fault.
challenge.answer: A line-to-neutral short on zone A trips the common protection. The two rockers are independent, but both get their feed through that device.

activities.instruction: Check the circuit with the control on.

expectedObservations.title: Cooker · reduced exercise load stops drawing power

activities.title: Turn the cooker isolator back on
activities.instruction: Turn Double-pole cooker switch on.
activities.explanation: Cooker · reduced exercise load draws power.

expectedObservations.title: Cooker · reduced exercise load draws power

activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Cooker · reduced exercise load · L and the black probe on Cooker · reduced exercise load · N. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Compare the incoming L–N voltage with L–N at the cooker. Use the protective-path test separately from the heating check. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Bench supply · PE and Cooker · reduced exercise load · PE. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?

Only the line contact moves

challenge.title: Diagnose: Cooker supply and double-pole isolation
challenge.briefing: The cooker heats but its earth check fails.
challenge.hint: Trace the PE wire from the board to the cooker’s earth terminal.
challenge.answer: The cooker’s protective conductor is open. Heating current still has its line and neutral path, so the cooker can appear to work normally.

challenge.title: Diagnose: S-plan two-port zone controls
challenge.briefing: With only the heating zone calling, its valve opens but the boiler stays off.
challenge.hint: Look for the boiler call as it leaves the heating valve’s END terminal, then check the common connection.
challenge.answer: The wire from the heating valve end switch to the boiler-call junction is open. The cylinder end switch can still call the boiler and mask the break.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply

activities.title: Turn down the thermostat in room A
activities.instruction: Turn Room A demand down.
activities.explanation: Manifold actuator A opens. Manifold actuator B closes. Manifold circulation pump draws power.

activities.instruction: Turn Room B demand down.
activities.explanation: Manifold circulation pump stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: Manifold circulation pump stops drawing power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Manifold circulation pump · L and the black probe on Manifold circulation pump · N. Record the volts.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Room A demand · OUT and Underfloor heating wiring centre · I1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: When should the shared pump stop in this circuit?

options.label: When neither room calls for heat
As soon as either room reaches temperature

challenge.answer: The wire from the room A thermostat to I1 is open. B still has its own signal and can run the shared pump.

activities.explanation: Up contactor closes. Down contactor opens.

challenge.answer: The wire from the upper limit output to auxiliary 21 on the down contactor is open. The up command never reaches the up coil.

activities.title: What do you expect?

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to Battery inverter with packaged backup changeover · L

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to Battery inverter with packaged backup changeover · PE

activities.title: Connect Battery inverter with packaged backup changeover · BL to Essential lighting on backup output · L

activities.title: Turn on the bench and local supplies
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply. Choose Battery inverter with packaged backup changeover and turn it on with Operate.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity. Solar and battery supplies have their own controls.

activities.title: Switch off the mains and try the backup supply
activities.instruction: Turn off the mains supply in the lab.
activities.explanation: Essential lighting on backup output draws power. Socket on mains only stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: Essential lighting on backup output draws power
Socket on mains only stops drawing power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Essential lighting on backup output · L and the black probe on Essential lighting on backup output · N. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Measure BL to BN and L to N on the ordinary branch during the outage. Battery charge and transfer are simplified in this exercise. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Battery inverter with packaged backup changeover · BN and Essential lighting on backup output · N. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.

activities.title: Why did that happen?

activities.title: Repair the fault

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Battery inverter and essential-load backup
challenge.briefing: The battery has energy, but the essential lamp goes out during a grid cut.
challenge.hint: Follow the complete pair from the backup output to the essential lamp.
challenge.answer: The wire from backup BN to lamp N is open. The lamp has no complete return to the backup source.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Check one load on each phase
activities.instruction: Check one load on each phase.
activities.explanation: Phase 1 to neutral demand draws power. Phase 2 to neutral demand draws power. Phase 3 to neutral demand draws power. Expect about 400 V between phases and 230 V from phase to neutral.

expectedObservations.title: Phase 1 to neutral demand draws power
Phase 2 to neutral demand draws power
Phase 3 to neutral demand draws power
Expect about 400 V between phases and 230 V from phase to neutral

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Phase 1 to neutral demand · L and the black probe on Phase 1 to neutral demand · N. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Between different phases expect about 400 V. From one phase to neutral expect about 231 V. A single phase-to-neutral reading cannot confirm all three phases. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Three-pole circuit breaker · 6 and Phase 3 to neutral demand · L. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Why are both 400 V and about 230 V correct readings on this board?
activities.explanation: Look for L1, L2 and N. On this bench, keep one probe on L1 and move the other from N to L2. The reading goes from about 230 V to 400 V.

options.label: They are different settings for the same pair of terminals
They are measured between different pairs of terminals

activities.title: Repair the fault

activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Three-phase board with phase-neutral loads
challenge.briefing: Two branches work and the third has lost power. The breaker handle is still on.
challenge.hint: Compare each phase at the breaker output with the corresponding load terminal.
challenge.answer: The line between the breaker’s L3 output and the third load is open. The other two branches still have their phase and neutral.

activities.title: Inspect DOL three-phase contactor
activities.instruction: Choose DOL three-phase contactor, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: A small coil pulls the main contacts closed to feed a larger load. Extra contacts can hold the coil on or signal that it has closed.

activities.title: Inspect Motor overload and NC control contact
activities.instruction: Choose Motor overload and NC control contact, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: If the motor draws too much current, the overload opens its small switch marked 95–96. In the starter circuit, that cuts power to the coil and stops the motor.

activities.instruction: Choose Three-phase motor · externally linked star, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: There are two ends to each of the three windings. The links between these six terminals set the motor for star or delta.

activities.title: Inspect Stop · normally closed
activities.instruction: Choose Stop · normally closed, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: The contacts change when you press the button and spring back when you let go.

activities.title: Inspect Start · momentary normally open

activities.explanation: The contacts change when you press the button and spring back when you let go.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: What does the contactor do after you let go of Start?
activities.explanation: The small holding contact keeps the coil on. The three main contacts carry the motor current. Stop opens the coil circuit and all the contacts release.

options.label: It stays pulled in

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1 with the phase L1 wire.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join DOL three-phase contactor · 2 to Motor overload and NC control contact · 1 with the phase L1 wire.

activities.title: Connect DOL three-phase contactor · 4 to Motor overload and NC control contact · 3

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join DOL three-phase contactor · 6 to Motor overload and NC control contact · 5 with the phase L3 wire.
activities.explanation: Outgoing side of the main contacts 5–6. When the coil pulls in, these two terminals join and can carry the load current. → Incoming side of 5–6. The overload checks motor current here. If it trips, 95–96 open. In the starter lesson that cuts power to the coil.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Three-phase motor · externally linked star · V2 to Three-phase motor · externally linked star · W2 with the output wire.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Three-pole circuit breaker · 2 to Stop · normally closed · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries phase 1 out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.title: Connect Stop · normally closed · NC to Motor overload and NC control contact · 95
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Stop · normally closed · NC to Motor overload and NC control contact · 95 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed. NC joins COM at rest. It opens while you hold the button down. → Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops.

activities.title: Connect Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Start · momentary normally open · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Motor overload and NC control contact · 96 to Start · momentary normally open · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. → Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. → Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go.

activities.explanation: Normally open. NO joins COM while you hold the button down. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect DOL three-phase contactor · 14 to DOL three-phase contactor · A1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join DOL three-phase contactor · 14 to DOL three-phase contactor · A1 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.instruction: Release Stop and check that the motor stays off.
activities.explanation: Three-phase motor · externally linked star stops drawing power. DOL three-phase contactor opens.

expectedObservations.title: Three-phase motor · externally linked star stops drawing power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and the black probe on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Put the probes on A1 and A2. Press Start, then let go. Does the coil still have voltage with your finger off the button? If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between DOL three-phase contactor · 14 and DOL three-phase contactor · A1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Which path keeps the coil powered after you let go?
activities.explanation: The small holding contact keeps the coil on. The three main contacts carry the motor current. Stop opens the coil circuit and all the contacts release.

options.label: A path through the open Start button
The path through the auxiliary holding contact

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Three-phase DOL motor starter
challenge.briefing: The motor starts, then stops as soon as you lift your finger.
challenge.hint: Follow the starter’s auxiliary output 14 back to coil A1.
challenge.answer: The wire from 14 back to A1 is broken. The Start button feeds the coil while you hold it. When you let go, there’s no feed to keep it on.

activities.title: Inspect 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral
activities.instruction: Choose 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: The three line terminals are L1, L2 and L3. At the 400 V setting, expect about 230 V from any one of them to neutral.

activities.title: Inspect Three-pole circuit breaker
activities.instruction: Choose Three-pole circuit breaker, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: One handle switches all three phases. If a fault trips one pole, all three open together.

activities.title: Inspect Forward contactor · mechanical pair
activities.instruction: Choose Forward contactor · mechanical pair, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: A small coil pulls the main contacts closed to feed a larger load. Extra contacts can hold the coil on or signal that it has closed.

activities.title: Inspect Reverse contactor · mechanical pair
activities.instruction: Choose Reverse contactor · mechanical pair, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: A small coil pulls the main contacts closed to feed a larger load. Extra contacts can hold the coil on or signal that it has closed.

activities.title: Inspect Common motor overload
activities.instruction: Choose Common motor overload, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: If the motor draws too much current, the overload opens its small switch marked 95–96. In the starter circuit, that cuts power to the coil and stops the motor.

activities.title: Inspect Reversible externally star-linked motor
activities.instruction: Choose Reversible externally star-linked motor, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: There are two ends to each of the three windings. The links between these six terminals set the motor for star or delta.

activities.title: Inspect Run contactor

activities.title: Inspect Stop · normally closed

activities.explanation: The contacts change when you press the button and spring back when you let go.

activities.title: Inspect Start · momentary normally open

activities.title: Inspect Forward / reverse selector

activities.explanation: Turn the selector to choose A or B. It stays there when you let go.

activities.title: What do you expect?

activities.title: Connect Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · 2 to Common motor overload · 1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · 2 to Common motor overload · 1 with the phase L1 wire.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · 6 to Common motor overload · 5 with the phase L3 wire.

activities.title: Connect Reversible externally star-linked motor · V2 to Reversible externally star-linked motor · W2

activities.title: Connect Three-pole circuit breaker · 2 to Stop · normally closed · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Three-pole circuit breaker · 2 to Stop · normally closed · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries phase 1 out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.title: Connect Stop · normally closed · NC to Common motor overload · 95
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Stop · normally closed · NC to Common motor overload · 95 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed. NC joins COM at rest. It opens while you hold the button down. → Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops.

activities.title: Connect Common motor overload · 96 to Start · momentary normally open · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Common motor overload · 96 to Start · momentary normally open · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. → Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.title: Connect Common motor overload · 96 to Run contactor · 13
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Common motor overload · 96 to Run contactor · 13 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed contacts 95–96. An overload trip opens them. When they are wired in series with the coil, the contactor drops out and the motor stops. → Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go.

activities.title: Connect Start · momentary normally open · NO to Run contactor · A1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Start · momentary normally open · NO to Run contactor · A1 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally open. NO joins COM while you hold the button down. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Run contactor · 14 to Run contactor · A1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Run contactor · 14 to Run contactor · A1 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Run contactor · A2
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Run contactor · A2 with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Run contactor · 14 to Forward / reverse selector · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Run contactor · 14 to Forward / reverse selector · COM with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally open auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 13 joins 14. Wired across Start, this pair can keep the coil on after you let go. → The feed comes into COM. The selector sends it to A or B.

activities.title: Connect Forward / reverse selector · A to Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · 21
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Forward / reverse selector · A to Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · 21 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: A joins COM in the first position. → Normally closed auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 21 separates from 22. In a reversing starter this can keep the other contactor off.

activities.title: Connect Forward / reverse selector · B to Forward contactor · mechanical pair · 21

activities.explanation: Normally closed auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 21 separates from 22. In a reversing starter this can keep the other contactor off. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect Forward contactor · mechanical pair · 22 to Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · A1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Forward contactor · mechanical pair · 22 to Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · A1 with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally closed auxiliary contacts. When the contactor pulls in, 21 separates from 22. In a reversing starter this can keep the other contactor off. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Interlocked forward/reverse motor starter
challenge.briefing: Forward is selected and Start operates the run circuit, but the forward contactor stays out.
challenge.hint: Trace the forward selector output into the reverse contactor’s normally closed auxiliary contact.
challenge.answer: The wire from selector A to reverse terminal 21 is open. The reverse contactor can be released and still have no forward command to pass through its interlock.

activities.title: Why did that happen?

challenge.title: Diagnose: Six-terminal star-delta motor starter
challenge.briefing: Star works during starting. At changeover it releases, but delta never pulls in.
challenge.hint: Follow the timer relay’s delta output through the star contactor’s normally closed interlock.
challenge.answer: The wire from the timer relay’s NO contact to star terminal 21 is open. When star releases, the delta coil still has no feed and the winding circuit is incomplete.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Switch off heater stage two
activities.instruction: Turn Stage B temperature demand down.
activities.explanation: Heater stage A closes. Heater stage B opens.

activities.title: Trip the cut-out for both heaters
activities.instruction: Open Independent high-temperature safety limit.
activities.explanation: Heater stage A opens. Heater stage B opens.

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Stage 1 phase 1 element · L and the black probe on Stage 1 phase 1 element · N. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Compare total power with one stage and with both. Check the stage coils to distinguish a single thermostat opening from the common high limit opening. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Stage B temperature demand · OUT and Heater stage B · A1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Both heater stages are on. Which ones stop if the cut-out opens?
activities.explanation: Each stage has its own control. Both share the high-temperature cut-out, so both heaters switch off if they get too hot.

options.label: Only the last stage switched on
Both heater stages

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Staged three-phase heater bank
challenge.briefing: Both stages call for heat, but only the first bank heats.
challenge.hint: Read the stage B thermostat output and the voltage at the second contactor coil.
challenge.answer: The wire from thermostat B to stage B coil A1 is open. The common limit still supplies stage A, so that bank continues to heat.

activities.title: Start the receiving belt

activities.title: Start the feed belt
activities.instruction: Press and release Start · momentary normally open. Watch what stays on.
activities.explanation: Downstream conveyor starter closes. Upstream conveyor starter closes.

activities.title: Check that both belts are running
activities.instruction: Check that both belts are running.
activities.explanation: Downstream conveyor starter closes. Upstream conveyor starter closes.

activities.instruction: Press and release Stop · normally closed. Watch what stays on.
activities.explanation: Downstream conveyor starter opens. Upstream conveyor starter opens.

activities.title: Stopping the downstream conveyor also stops the one feeding it
activities.instruction: Stopping the downstream conveyor also stops the one feeding it.
activities.explanation: Downstream conveyor starter opens. Upstream conveyor starter opens.

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and the black probe on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Compare the receiving starter’s feedback output with the control feed at the second starter. Check the coils as well as the motor states. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Downstream conveyor starter · 14 and Stop · normally closed · COM. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Why does stopping the receiving conveyor also stop the feed belt?
activities.explanation: The feed belt needs a closed contact from the receiving belt’s starter. When the receiving belt stops, that contact opens.

options.label: Both motors are connected to the same starter output
Its starter contact opens the feed belt’s control path

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Sequential two-motor conveyor control
challenge.briefing: The receiving belt runs. The feed belt still refuses to start.
challenge.hint: Follow auxiliary terminal 14 on the receiving starter towards the upstream station’s Stop contact.
challenge.answer: The wire from the receiving starter’s 14 to the feed conveyor’s Stop COM is open. The first motor runs, but its run signal cannot reach the second starter.

activities.title: Inspect 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral

activities.title: Inspect Three-pole circuit breaker

activities.title: Inspect Normal pumping level

activities.title: Inspect Pump A starter

activities.title: Connect Isolated 24 V control supply · - to Controller secondary status · N

activities.title: Read the current in one wire

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Workpiece-present sensor · OUT and PLC · 24 V controller · I1. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?

activities.explanation: Trace the two sensor wires to I1 and I2 on the PLC. Both inputs have to be on before its output Q1 can start the motor.

options.label: Either input can turn the output on by itself

challenge.title: Diagnose: PLC inputs and motor starter
challenge.briefing: The PLC is on and both sensors are on, but the motor never gets a run command.
challenge.hint: Compare the signal leaving the presence sensor with I1 at the controller.
challenge.answer: The wire from the presence sensor to I1 is broken. The PLC needs both I1 and I2 on before it starts the motor. Watch I1 as you operate the sensor.

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and the black probe on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Compare the safety relay’s armed state with the motor coil state. When the contactor is released, check the feedback path used before resetting the relay. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L1 to Three-pole circuit breaker · 1. Record the amps.

activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Machine motor contactor · 22 and Safety relay · FB. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: What did Reset do in this circuit?
activities.explanation: A small contact tells the safety relay when the motor contactor has let go. Once the safety circuit is ready, Reset allows a fresh start. The motor waits until you press Start.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Safety relay and contactor feedback
challenge.briefing: The machine is stopped and both safety inputs are healthy. Pressing Reset does not arm the relay.
challenge.hint: With the starter released, follow the wire from terminal 22 back to FB on the safety relay.
challenge.answer: The wire from starter terminal 22 to feedback input FB is open. The relay cannot confirm a released contactor before arming. Check this in the stopped, unarmed state.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Light a cupboard when its door opens

challenge.answer: There’s a break between B on the selector and CLOSE on the valve. The wire to OPEN is still sound, so the valve can travel one way.

activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 24 V isolated DC driver · - to instrument indicator · − with the negative (−) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. → Negative LED return on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver.

activities.title: Connect Positive distribution connector · 3 to beacon branch carrier · 1 A · IN
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Positive distribution connector · 3 to beacon branch carrier · 1 A · IN with the positive (+) wire.
activities.explanation: Terminal 3. All four holes on this block share a metal link. Wires connected here meet inside the block. → Paired with OUT. Opening this device breaks the connection between IN and OUT.

activities.title: Connect beacon branch carrier · 1 A · OUT to beacon indicator · +
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join beacon branch carrier · 1 A · OUT to beacon indicator · + with the positive (+) wire.
activities.explanation: Paired with IN. Opening this device breaks the connection between IN and OUT. → Positive LED input on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver.

activities.title: Connect 24 V isolated DC driver · - to beacon indicator · −
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 24 V isolated DC driver · - to beacon indicator · − with the negative (−) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. → Negative LED return on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Remove the beacon fuse
activities.instruction: Open beacon branch carrier.
activities.explanation: beacon indicator stops drawing power. instrument indicator draws power.

activities.title: Put the beacon fuse back
activities.instruction: Close beacon branch carrier.
activities.explanation: beacon indicator draws power. instrument indicator draws power.

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on instrument indicator · + and the black probe on instrument indicator · −. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Leave the warning light connected. With the fuse carrier open, put the black probe on − and check each side of the carrier with the red probe. The supply side still reads about 24 V. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between beacon branch carrier · 1 A · OUT and beacon indicator · +. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: Why does the instrument still have 24 V?
activities.explanation: Follow the two wires from the fuses. One goes to the instrument and the other goes to the beacon. Opening the beacon fuse leaves the instrument on.

options.label: Its current passes through the open beacon fuse
It has a separate fused branch

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Open one fuse on a 24 V supply
challenge.briefing: The beacon stays dark with its fuse carrier closed.
challenge.hint: Close the beacon fuse. Compare the voltage at its outgoing terminal with voltage at the beacon.
challenge.answer: The wire from the beacon fuse output to the beacon is open. The instrument is on a separate fused branch and can still work.

title: Build an entrance call and courtesy light

circuit.name: Build an entrance call and courtesy light

components.label: 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V

activities.title: Inspect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V
activities.instruction: Choose 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: This is where power enters the bench. Follow the line, neutral and earth from here.

activities.title: Inspect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA
activities.instruction: Choose Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: This breaker protects one circuit. It can trip on too much current or when some current returns by another path.

activities.title: Inspect 12 V AC bell transformer
activities.instruction: Choose 12 V AC bell transformer, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: The supply goes to the first winding. The second winding feeds a separate circuit. Measure across its two ends to read the output voltage.

activities.title: Inspect 24 V isolated DC driver
activities.instruction: Choose 24 V isolated DC driver, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: This driver supplies the LEDs with a steady DC voltage. Look for + and − on the output.

activities.title: Inspect Entrance bell push
activities.instruction: Choose Entrance bell push, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: Hold the button to ring the bell. Let go and the two contacts spring apart. The two screw terminals on the back are interchangeable.

activities.title: Inspect Entrance AC chime
activities.instruction: Choose Entrance AC chime, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: The chime sounds when there is power across its two screws. In the bell circuit, pressing a door button completes that path.

activities.title: Inspect Changeover relay
activities.instruction: Choose Changeover relay, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: Power the coil and the relay changes which contacts touch. The coil and contacts have separate connections.

activities.title: Inspect Courtesy light
activities.instruction: Choose Courtesy light, then Show terminals. Pick a terminal to see what connects there.
activities.explanation: The driver feeds this light. Look for the positive and negative marks on the low-voltage side.

activities.title: What do you expect?
activities.instruction: The lamp return wire breaks. What should still work when a visitor presses the button?
activities.explanation: Pressing the button powers the relay coil. Its contact closes the lamp’s DC circuit without joining the supplies.

options.label: Only the courtesy lamp
The bell and the relay coil

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1 with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L. → Top 1 takes the line feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked 2.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · N to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Supply
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · N to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Supply with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on. → Top N takes the neutral feed in this circuit. With the handle on, it connects to the bottom terminal marked N.

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to 12 V AC bell transformer · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to 12 V AC bell transformer · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load to 12 V AC bell transformer · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load to 12 V AC bell transformer · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom N carries neutral out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked N. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to 12 V AC bell transformer · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to 12 V AC bell transformer · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to 24 V isolated DC driver · L
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 2 to 24 V isolated DC driver · L with the line (L) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom 2 carries line out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked 1. → Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

activities.title: Connect Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load to 24 V isolated DC driver · N
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · N · Load to 24 V isolated DC driver · N with the neutral (N) wire.
activities.explanation: Bottom N carries neutral out to the circuit. Switching off breaks its connection to the top terminal marked N. → Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

activities.title: Connect Bench supply · PE to 24 V isolated DC driver · PE
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Bench supply · PE to 24 V isolated DC driver · PE with the earth (PE) wire.
activities.explanation: Supply earth. The earth connection runs alongside the meter. → Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

activities.title: Connect 12 V AC bell transformer · SEC 1 to Entrance bell push · Top screw
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 12 V AC bell transformer · SEC 1 to Entrance bell push · Top screw with the output wire.
activities.explanation: AC secondary, marked SEC 1. These are the two ends of the output winding. Use AC volts and put one probe on SEC 1 and one on SEC 2. → Either wire can go here. Press the button and the top and bottom screws are connected.

activities.title: Connect Entrance bell push · Bottom screw to Entrance AC chime · 1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Entrance bell push · Bottom screw to Entrance AC chime · 1 with the output wire.
activities.explanation: Either wire can go here. Press the button and the top and bottom screws are connected. → First connection on the sounder. The bell lessons use AC from a transformer. The door alarm uses DC. Look at the supply marking before choosing a meter setting.

activities.title: Connect 12 V AC bell transformer · SEC 2 to Entrance AC chime · 2
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 12 V AC bell transformer · SEC 2 to Entrance AC chime · 2 with the output wire.
activities.explanation: AC secondary, marked SEC 2. These are the two ends of the output winding. Use AC volts and put one probe on SEC 1 and one on SEC 2. → Second connection on the sounder. The bell lessons use AC from a transformer. The door alarm uses DC. Look at the supply marking before choosing a meter setting.

activities.title: Connect Entrance bell push · Bottom screw to Changeover relay · A1
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Entrance bell push · Bottom screw to Changeover relay · A1 with the output wire.
activities.explanation: Either wire can go here. Press the button and the top and bottom screws are connected. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect 12 V AC bell transformer · SEC 2 to Changeover relay · A2
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 12 V AC bell transformer · SEC 2 to Changeover relay · A2 with the output wire.
activities.explanation: AC secondary, marked SEC 2. These are the two ends of the output winding. Use AC volts and put one probe on SEC 1 and one on SEC 2. → One end of the coil. Measure across A1–A2 to see what voltage reaches it. The load has its own contacts.

activities.title: Connect 24 V isolated DC driver · + to Changeover relay · COM
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 24 V isolated DC driver · + to Changeover relay · COM with the positive (+) wire.
activities.explanation: Positive output of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. → Common terminal. Moving the contact joins COM to either NC or NO.

activities.title: Connect Changeover relay · NO to Courtesy light · +
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join Changeover relay · NO to Courtesy light · + with the control wire.
activities.explanation: Normally open. NO joins COM while the coil is on. → Positive LED input on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver.

activities.title: Connect 24 V isolated DC driver · - to Courtesy light · −
activities.instruction: With all supplies off, join 24 V isolated DC driver · - to Courtesy light · − with the negative (−) wire.
activities.explanation: Negative output return of the isolated DC supply. Measure between + and −. Keep the DC return separate from mains neutral. → Negative LED return on this low-voltage light. It takes power from the DC driver.

activities.title: Turn on the bench supply
activities.instruction: Set the meter to volts, then turn on the bench supply.
activities.explanation: Use voltage mode to check a powered circuit. Switch off all sources before testing continuity.

activities.title: Press the entrance push
activities.instruction: Hold Entrance bell push down.
activities.explanation: Entrance AC chime draws power. Changeover relay closes. Courtesy light draws power. The bell and the light still have separate supplies.

expectedObservations.title: The bell and the light still have separate supplies

activities.title: Release the entrance push
activities.instruction: Release Entrance bell push.
activities.explanation: Entrance AC chime stops drawing power. Changeover relay opens. Courtesy light stops drawing power.

expectedObservations.title: Entrance AC chime stops drawing power

activities.title: Check the voltage
activities.instruction: Put the red probe on Courtesy light · + and the black probe on Courtesy light · −. Record the volts.
activities.explanation: Leave the tester on V. Across the bell supply it reads AC. Across the lamp it reads DC. Keep both probes on the same circuit. If you see zero, check the switch position.

activities.title: Read the current in one wire
activities.instruction: Choose the wire from Bench supply · L to Circuit breaker (RCBO) · 16 A / 30 mA · 1. Record the amps.
activities.explanation: The meter shows the current in this wire. Where the circuit splits, the branches can carry different currents.

activities.title: Check the wire for a break
activities.instruction: Turn off all sources, then measure resistance between Changeover relay · NO and Courtesy light · +. Take the meter out of resistance mode before switching the power back on.
activities.explanation: A low resistance shows a path between the probes. If two wires reach the same point, the meter can still find a path around a break.

activities.title: Why did that happen?
activities.instruction: How can the bell button also switch the light?
activities.explanation: Pressing the button powers the relay coil. Its contact closes the lamp’s DC circuit without joining the supplies.

options.label: The button powers the relay coil and its contact switches the light
The bell and lamp share a return wire

activities.title: Repair the fault
activities.instruction: Use your readings to find what went wrong. Repair it, then reset any device that tripped.
activities.explanation: Run a fresh test to check the repair.

activities.title: Test the repair
activities.instruction: Choose Test circuit to check your repair.
activities.explanation: The bench tries the lesson controls again using your wiring.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Build an entrance call and courtesy light
challenge.briefing: The bell rings and the relay operates but the courtesy light remains dark.
challenge.hint: Hold the entrance push. If the bell and relay operate, follow the DC side from the relay contact to the courtesy lamp.
challenge.answer: The wire from the relay’s NO contact to the courtesy lamp is open. The AC bell and coil still have their own complete circuit.
